home.title: Kaeri · an open-source anime client
home.description: An open-source anime client with native apps for Mac, iPhone, iPad, Android, Android TV, Windows and Linux, and a terminal app.
home.hero.title: Kaeri, on every screen.
home.hero.sub: One anime app, native on Mac, iPhone and iPad, and on Android, Android TV, Windows, Linux and the terminal too.
home.hero.caption: The Mac, iPad and iPhone apps.
home.hero.macAlt: The Mac app on Home: Stardust Wayfarer in the spotlight with a button to resume episode 7, a Continue row of four shows, and this week’s calendar

faq.title: Before you install.
faq.shows.q: Does Kaeri come with any shows?
faq.shows.a: It starts with a demo of Creative Commons works. Everything else comes from sources you add: a media server, your own files, or plugins from a plugin store you trust.
faq.mac.q: Why does my Mac ask before it opens Kaeri?
faq.mac.a: The Mac app isn’t notarised by Apple, so macOS asks once. Choose Done, then Open Anyway in System Settings, under Privacy & Security.
faq.store.q: Why isn’t it on the App Store?
faq.store.a: The App Store needs a paid developer account. The iPhone and iPad app installs through SideStore or AltStore instead, and they refresh it every seven days on a free Apple ID.
faq.account.a: No. Browsing needs no account, and devices on the same Wi-Fi sync with each other without one. Sign in to AniList, MyAnimeList, Kitsu, Simkl or Trakt if you want your progress on a tracker.
faq.cost.a: No. Kaeri is free and MIT licensed on every platform.

download.title: Download Kaeri
download.description: Download the Kaeri apps for Mac, iPhone, iPad, Android, Android TV, Windows and Linux, and the terminal app.
download.steps.title: Install steps.
download.steps.text: The apps aren’t in any app store, so the first install takes one extra step. After that they update themselves.

download.check.title: Check a download.
download.check.text: Every file in a release has a .sha256 beside it. Put both in one folder and run:
download.older.title: Older versions.
download.older.text: Every release stays on GitHub with its files, checksums and notes.
download.steps.mac.needs: macOS 26 or later, on Apple silicon.
download.steps.mac.list:
• Open the disk image and drag Kaeri to Applications.
  • Open Kaeri. When macOS says it cannot verify the app, choose Done.
  • In System Settings › Privacy & Security, choose Open Anyway beside the line about Kaeri, and confirm with your password or Touch ID.
download.steps.mac.note: The app is signed without an Apple developer account, so it isn’t notarised. Updates from inside the app don’t ask again. From a terminal, xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Kaeri.app does the same as Open Anyway.
download.steps.ios.list:
• Set up SideStore or AltStore on the device, as its own guide describes.
  • In Sources, choose + and paste this address:{{code}}
  • Install Kaeri from the source.
  • If iOS asks for Developer Mode, turn it on under Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode and restart.
download.steps.ios.note: With a free Apple ID the signature lasts seven days, so SideStore or AltStore has to refresh the app within that time. Your data stays either way.
download.steps.android.list:
• Download the APK on the phone or tablet and open it.
  • Android asks once whether your browser or file manager may install apps. Allow it, go back and choose Install.
download.steps.android.note: Each release installs over the one before and keeps your data. Play Protect may offer to scan it, since it isn’t on Google Play.
download.steps.android-tv.needs: Android TV or Google TV 11 or later, on ARM.
download.steps.android-tv.arch: Most TV boxes run a 32-bit system and take the armv7 file. Newer boxes take arm64. If the install says the app isn’t compatible, try the other one.
download.steps.android-tv.list:
• Install Downloader from Google Play on the TV.
  • In Downloader, enter github.com/bitknox/kaeri/releases/latest and choose the file under Assets.
  • Allow Downloader to install apps, go back and choose Install.
download.steps.android-tv.note: You can also install it from a computer with adb, as the installation guide describes. After that the TV app updates itself.
download.steps.windows.list:
• Run the installer. It installs for your account only, so it asks for no administrator password.
  • When Windows says “Windows protected your PC”, choose More info.
  • Choose Run anyway.
download.steps.windows.note: A new release installs over the one before and keeps your library and settings.
download.steps.linux.needs: Ubuntu 25.04 or later, including 26.04 LTS, Fedora 42 or Debian 13. The AppImage needs glibc 2.41.
download.steps.linux.list: • Make the file executable once, then open it:{{code}}
download.steps.linux.note: It carries GTK 4, libadwaita and the player, so there is nothing to install first. On Ubuntu 24.04 and other older systems, use the terminal app.
download.steps.terminal.needs: macOS, Linux and Windows. It needs mpv and ffmpeg.
download.steps.terminal.list:
• Install mpv and ffmpeg. The .deb does this for you.{{code}}
  • Download the installer for your system from the latest release: a .pkg on macOS, setup.exe on Windows or a .deb on Debian and Ubuntu. There is also an AppImage for other distros, and an archive for putting the binary on your PATH yourself.
  • Run it, then type kaeri in a terminal.
download.steps.terminal.note: Once it’s installed, kaeri --update keeps it current. On a Mac it shares its history and settings with the Mac app.
features.title: Kaeri features
features.description: Every Kaeri feature, and which app has each one.
features.hero.title: Kaeri knows where you stopped.
features.hero.sub: Apps for Mac, iPhone, iPad, Android, Android TV, Windows and Linux, and one for the terminal.
features.hero.caption: The Mac app.
features.hero.alt: The Mac app on Home: the show in progress in the spotlight, the rows rolling up, then a show picked from a row and its title page opening
features.find.title: Search and the calendar.
features.find.lead: Browse by genre, year and season without an account, or follow the seasonal charts and the week’s calendar.
features.find.text: A ~ marks an estimated air time, and a Dub tag marks an episode already dubbed.
features.find.caption: The Mac app and the iPhone app.
features.find.searchAlt: The Mac app’s search, with a query, its two results and the filters panel open: genres, tags, years and length
features.find.calendarAlt: The iPhone app’s calendar: the week’s days, then each day’s episodes with their times
features.player.title: Upscaled as it plays.
features.player.lead: Episodes play in mpv, upscaled by ArtCNN or Anime4K, with the opening and ending marked on the seek bar.
features.player.text: Drag the line to compare a 480p stream.
features.player.caption: From こうしす！ #3.2 by OPAP-JP contributors, CC BY 4.0.
features.found.title: Finds the opening by itself.
features.found.lead: When AniSkip has no times for an episode, Kaeri compares its audio with the show’s earlier episodes on your device and finds the opening and ending.
features.found.text: Found times get the Skip button, and once you confirm them or skip them twice, they skip by themselves like any others. Finding pauses in power saving mode and when storage runs low.
features.found.caption: The Android TV app, checking the edges of an opening it found. If you share skip times with AniSkip, Kaeri asks once per show whether the edges were right.
features.found.alt: Close up of the Android TV app’s player: Hoshikuzu no Tabibito, episode 7, with the opening marked on the seek bar, and a panel with its start at 1:31, its end at 3:00 and the line Kaeri found these times from the audio
features.together.title: Watch together, and talk.
features.together.lead: Start a party and send the link. Everyone’s player stays in step, with chat and reactions in the room.
features.together.text: Each person plays from their own sources, and the party runs on a Syncplay server you choose.
features.together.caption: The Android app in a watch party. The picture is from こうしす！ #3.1 by OPAP-JP contributors, CC BY 4.0.
features.together.alt: The Android app playing an episode in a watch party: Mika’s chat line in the corner, the four reaction buttons down the side, your own laugh, and a man in a suit with his name card
features.sync.title: Sync without an account.
features.sync.lead: Pair your devices on the same Wi-Fi, or add a cloud folder you already use, and your history, resume points and lists stay the same on each.
features.sync.text: Changes are sealed so only your devices can read them, and Kaeri runs no server for it. Your trackers still get each change in order, even after a week offline.
features.sync.caption: The Mac app’s Devices settings. A cloud folder can be in Dropbox, OneDrive, Nextcloud, a WebDAV server or a folder on the device, and in Google Drive on Apple devices and Android phones and tablets.
features.sync.alt: Close up of the Mac app’s Devices settings: Kim’s iPhone, Living room TV and Kitchen iPad under Your devices, a sync note, a Google Drive cloud folder and the recovery key
features.tv.title: Your phone is the TV remote.
features.tv.lead: Send an episode to the Android TV app, then pause, seek and switch subtitles from your phone.
features.tv.text: The Mac, iPhone, iPad, Android, Windows and Linux apps all work as the remote.
features.tv.caption: The iPhone app as the remote, and the Android TV app.
features.tv.remoteAlt: The iPhone app as the TV’s remote: the episode playing, play and seek buttons, subtitles, audio and the TV’s volume
features.tv.tvAlt: The Android TV app on a title page, with a button to resume episode 7 and the episode list
features.plugins.title: You choose the sources.
features.plugins.lead: Sources are plugins, and each one can reach only the hosts it lists.
features.plugins.text: Run a store for your own plugins and your own devices. Every device you add gets a token of its own.
features.plugins.diagram: How a plugin store gives each device a token
features.also.title: And a lot of small things.
features.matrix.title: Where the apps differ.
features.matrix.text: All eight apps have search with filters, the calendar, seasonal charts, trailers, subtitle and audio tracks, skip, resume, Up next and watch parties. They all sync between your devices and with AniList, Simkl and Trakt, join plugin stores and play torrents. The table shows where they differ.
features.matrix.caption: Which app does each feature
features.matrix.note: Play on TV from the terminal app is in development, and so are home screen widgets on Windows.
